Travelling Users, VPN-Wechsel und Mobile-Carriers (CGNAT) erzeugen False Positives — Allowlist für bekannte Pendel-Routen oder Korrelation mit Entra ID Identity Protection RiskySignIns empfohlen. Bei breiter Adoption von Conditional Access Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) sinkt die Token-Lifetime und damit die Trefferquote dieses Musters.

title: NTLM Relay / Pass-the-Hash — Lateral Movement über mehrere Ziele (CVE-2026-32202)
description: Erkennt typisches Muster nach erfolgreichem NTLM-Hash-Leak (z.B. via LLMNR/NBT-NS-Poisoning oder CVE-2026-32202): ein Account authentifiziert sich per NTLM-Network-Logon innerhalb von 30 Minuten gegen mehr als drei unterschiedliche Geräte — starkes Indiz für Pass-the-Hash oder NTLM-Relay-Aktivität.
kql:
DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where LogonType == "Network" and Protocol == "Ntlm"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where isnotempty(AccountName)
| summarize
    TargetCount = dcount(DeviceName),
    Targets = make_set(DeviceName, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by AccountName, AccountDomain, bin(Timestamp, 30m)
| where TargetCount > 3
| extend RiskSignal = "Possible NTLM Lateral Movement / Pass-the-Hash"
| order by TargetCount desc
author: Microsoft (adapted)
tuning_notes: Service-Accounts und Vulnerability-Scanner (z.B. Qualys, Defender for Identity Sensors) erzeugen legitime breit gefächerte NTLM-Network-Logons — diese vorab per Allowlist auf AccountName ausschließen. Schwelle TargetCount > 3 in 30m ist konservativ; in größeren AD-Umgebungen mit File-Server-Quervernetzung ggf. auf > 5 anheben. Computer-Accounts (endswith "$") werden bewusst ausgeschlossen, da Kerberos/NTLM-Replikation FP-Storm erzeugt. Für PtH-spezifische Signale ergänzend AlertEvidence/AlertInfo mit Title contains "Suspected pass-the-hash" aus Defender for Identity korrelieren.

title: AiTM Token Theft via Phishing Proxy — Token-Replay über mehrere IPs/Locations (15m-Fenster)
description: Erkennt Session-Token-Diebstahl nach AiTM-Phishing: erfolgreiche Sign-Ins desselben Users in derselben App, die innerhalb eines 15-Minuten-Fensters von mehr als einer IP UND mehr als einer Location erfolgen, korreliert mit Non-Interactive Sign-Ins (typisches Token-Replay-Muster, da gestohlene Cookies oft Refresh-Tokens auslösen). Strenger als KQL-T1111-001 — fokussiert auf gleichzeitige Sessions in engem Zeitfenster.
kql:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ResultType == 0
| summarize IPs = dcount(IPAddress), Locations = dcount(Location) by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where IPs > 1 and Locations > 1
| join kind=inner (
    AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where ResultType == 0
    | project UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, UserAgent
) on UserPrincipalName
author: Microsoft (adapted)
tuning_notes: Härten via Conditional Access: Token Protection (Preview) und Compliant Device Requirement aktivieren — beides reduziert die Replay-Wirksamkeit gestohlener Cookies. False Positives durch CGNAT, VPN-Wechsel oder Roaming-Mobilgeräte sind möglich; Allowlist auf bekannte Pendel-Routen oder Korrelation mit Entra ID Identity Protection RiskySignIns empfohlen. Der join auf UserPrincipalName ohne Zeitkorrelation kann bei vielen Non-Interactive Logins zu Fan-Out führen — bei Performance-Issues zusätzlich auf bin(TimeGenerated, 15m) im inneren Query joinen.

title: Linux Privilege Escalation Post-Exploit (CVE-2026-31431) — cp --no-preserve auf Azure Linux VMs/AKS
description: Erkennt typisches Post-Exploit-Pattern nach erfolgreicher CVE-2026-31431-Ausnutzung auf Azure Linux VMs und AKS-Nodes: Aufruf von /bin/cp mit Flag --no-preserve durch nicht-root-Account, was beim Kopieren von SUID-Binaries oder Konfigdateien Owner/Permission-Reset und damit indirekte Privilege Escalation ermöglicht.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where FileName == "cp" and FolderPath has "/bin/"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--no-preserve"
| where AccountName != "root" and isnotempty(AccountName)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, AccountDomain, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
author: Microsoft (adapted)
tuning_notes: Original-Query nutzte Windows SecurityEvent (EventID 4688) — auf Linux nicht vorhanden. Adaptiert auf MDE for Linux DeviceProcessEvents. FolderPath-Filter '/bin/' schließt Windows-Devices und ungewöhnliche Pfade aus. Falls auch andere Pfade relevant sind (z.B. /usr/bin/cp), Filter erweitern. CI/CD-Pipelines und Container-Build-Skripte auf AKS-Nodes können legitime --no-preserve-Aufrufe enthalten — Allowlist via InitiatingProcessFileName (z.B. dockerd, containerd-shim) empfohlen. Bei Treffern parallel DeviceFileEvents auf SUID-Files (chmod u+s) für vollständige Exploit-Chain prüfen.

title: ClickFix Chain Correlation: Proxy Execution + AppData Persistence + Defender Tamper
description: High-confidence correlation for a ClickFix intrusion (Huntress: Potemkin loader / RMMProject). Each leg is individually noisy – pcalua-proxied mshta/msiexec, a Run-key write into AppData, and Set-MpPreference/Stop-Service WinDefend all occur in benign administration. This rule fires only when all three land on the same DeviceId within a 30-minute window, which does not happen in normal operations. The fidelity comes from the join, not any single leg.
kql:
let lookback = 3d;
let proxyChain = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "pcalua.exe" and FileName in~ ("mshta.exe", "msiexec.exe")
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, ProxyTime = Timestamp, ProxyCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
let runKey = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
    | where RegistryKey has "CurrentVersion" and RegistryKey has "Run"
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("AppData", "ProgramData")
    | project DeviceId, KeyTime = Timestamp, RegistryValueData;
let defenderTamper = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-MpPreference", "Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath", "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "Stop-Service WinDefend")
    | project DeviceId, TamperTime = Timestamp, TamperCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
proxyChain
| join kind=inner runKey on DeviceId
| join kind=inner defenderTamper on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('minute', ProxyTime, KeyTime)) <= 30
    and abs(datetime_diff('minute', ProxyTime, TamperTime)) <= 30
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, ProxyTime, ProxyCmd, KeyTime, RegistryValueData, TamperTime, TamperCmd, chain = "ClickFix->Loader->DefenderTamper"
| sort by ProxyTime asc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Widen the 30m window if the operator spaces the legs out; narrow it to cut FPs in noisy admin environments. Add a first-leg anchor (unsigned/AppData process creation) to raise precision. Worthless on an unmonitored endpoint – the join needs the on-device telemetry that patient zero lacked.

title: pcalua.exe Proxying mshta/msiexec (ClickFix LOLBin Chain)
description: Detects the ClickFix LOLBin proxy chain where the signed Program Compatibility Assistant launcher pcalua.exe spawns mshta.exe or msiexec.exe. Using pcalua as the parent breaks the explorer/browser -> mshta ancestry that most rules key on, and lets a remote HTA silently pull and install an MSI (Potemkin loader). Covers kill-chain steps 2–3.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "pcalua.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("mshta.exe", "msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp asc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Key on the pcalua -> mshta|msiexec parent/child edge, not on mshta/msiexec alone. A renamed mshta/msiexec evades the FileName match – corroborate with the remote HTA/MSI URL on the command line and the follow-on drop under AppData\\Local.

title: Run Key Persistence Pointing to AppData/ProgramData Executable
description: Surfaces HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\\Run (and RunOnce) value writes whose data points at an executable under AppData or ProgramData – the persistence Potemkin's MSI installs (Run\\RunSearch -> AppData\\Local RunSearch.exe). Medium fidelity alone; primarily a correlation input for the ClickFix chain rule.
kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where ActionType == "RegistryValueSet"
| where RegistryKey has "CurrentVersion" and RegistryKey has "Run"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("AppData", "ProgramData")
| where RegistryValueData has ".exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Timestamp asc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: Many legitimate updaters and sync clients auto-start from AppData – expect volume, hence hunting not detection. Tighten by joining to a recent unsigned/AppData process creation on the same device, or allowlist known-good value data.

title: Microsoft Defender Teardown: Set-MpPreference / Exclusions / Service Stop
description: Detects the staged Defender teardown seen in the Potemkin ClickFix intrusion: Set-MpPreference toggles (real-time, IOAV, behavior, script), Add-MpPreference exclusion paths, and WinDefend/wscsvc/SecurityHealthService service stops or start=disabled. Maps to ATT&CK v19 T1685 (Disable or Modify Tools, tactic Defense Impairment) – the legacy T1562.001 no longer exists in v19.1.
kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Set-MpPreference", "Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath",
    "DisableRealtimeMonitoring", "DisableIOAVProtection", "DisableBehaviorMonitoring", "DisableScriptScanning",
    "Stop-Service WinDefend", "config WinDefend start= disabled", "Stop-Service wscsvc", "Stop-Service SecurityHealthService")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp asc
author: triathIC
tuning_notes: FP: AV migrations and legitimate IT maintenance touch these controls. The tell is the SEQUENCE (toggles -> exclusion -> service stop) on one host in minutes, ideally right after an AppData-resident process appeared. FN: the in-memory AMSI patch never hits a command line, so this catches the PowerShell/sc.exe legs, not the patch.
